name: Hive Active Plug (UK)

radios.note: Zigbee to the Hive Hub; it doesn't join Wi-Fi itself. UK/Ireland type G plug.

matter.note: Hive's plug pages don't mention Matter, and we found no CSA listing for it.

apple_home.note: Hive's support site lists Hive Plugs for Apple Home, enabled from the Hive app via the Hive Hub. Schedules and Actions can't be controlled from the Home app. A retailer listing says no HomeKit; Hive's own pages say yes.

google_home.note: Hive lists Google Assistant; the plug reaches it through the Hive Hub and Hive account.

alexa.note: Through the Hive Alexa skill and the Hive Hub. Hive says the Alexa link doesn't support multi-user or multi-home setups.

smartthings.note: No official Hive or SmartThings page covers it. SmartThings forum users report mixed results pairing it directly over Zigbee.

home_assistant.note: Home Assistant's official Hive integration lists the Active Plug as a switch. It uses your Hive account (owner login, 2FA on) and the Hive Hub.

hubRequired.note: Needs a Hive Hub; Hive says first-time Hive buyers must buy one. Existing Hive users can add it to their current hub.

localControl.note: We found no Hive statement on control without the internet.

energyMonitoring.note: The Hive app shows the plugged-in appliance's power draw in watts. 'Hive Plug' is Hive's current name for the Active Plug (same shop page and spec URL).

maxLoadWatts.note: Hive's pages don't give a load rating. UK retailers list it as 13 A, but no official wattage figure was found.

summary: If you're new to Hive, budget for a Hive Hub: the Hive Active Plug is a UK Zigbee plug that reaches Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa and Home Assistant only through that hub. Existing Hive users can add it to the hub they already have. The Hive app shows the plugged-in appliance's power draw in watts. Neither Hive nor SmartThings documents SmartThings support.
caveats: Needs a Hive Hub; the plug can't join Wi-Fi on its own.
Schedules and Actions can't be controlled from Apple's Home app.
Hive's Alexa link doesn't support multi-user or multi-home setups.
Home Assistant needs the Hive account owner's login with two-factor authentication on.
UK/Ireland type G plug only, and Hive doesn't publish a load rating.
